notes:
Exec summary: Arcadia IDEFlow is building an editor-native copilot (VSCode + JetBrains plugin) targeted at enterprise developer teams. Primary pain: UX stutters and unpredictable suggestion timing when users type rapidly. They're evaluating Redwood for low-latency streaming + token-budget tuning to hit strict TTFT/first-token SLAs and reduce jitter.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-02-20: Intro call (Priya) — overview of Redwood product lines, asked for example latency profiles.
- 2026-02-27: Tech deep-dive (Marco + Infra team) — internal architecture: plugin streams to backend, server-side caching + per-user KV. Mentioned need for per-session model pinning and deterministic fallback.
- 2026-03-04: POC demo (Fireflies id ff_2026-03-04_ideflow_poc_demo) — integrated Redwood SDK into alpha plugin, ran a 10k-request synthetic workload. Observed median first-token 78ms, p95 410ms. Root cause: KV cache cold-starts + occasional GPU scheduling jitter.
- 2026-03-06: Security review kickoff — requested SOC2 cert + KMS integration details.
- 2026-03-09: Business sync (Priya + CFO) — procurement questions, interested in dedicated pool pricing and 6-month commit.

Use-case / requirements (high level):
- Workload: ultra-low latency inline completion + longer multi-line code synthesis.
- TTFT target: <= 120ms median, p99 < 250ms for single-line completions.
- Jitter tolerance: < 30ms median jitter, need mechanisms to smooth out tail spikes.
- Throughput: bursty typing patterns; per-team peak ~120 concurrent users, global ~1.2k daily active devs.
- Token budget tuning: want auto-budgeting (per-request token cap) that prioritizes first-token speed and aborts/condenses long generations when budget exceeded.
- Backpressure: client should gracefully degrade (send shorter prompts / low-latency fallback model) rather than time out.
- Model/version pinning: deterministic rollouts, canary to 5% -> 25% with automatic rollback on RTT or quality regression.
- Fallback policies: prefer quantized, faster 7B model on network degradation, but must preserve hallucination thresholds.

Technical asks for Redwood POC:
- Run TTFT microbench (100k synthetic inline completions) with Dedicated GPU pool, include cold-start scenarios and cache warm periods.
- Provide Optimize recommendations for batching/caching and suggested quantization profiles for their service pattern.
- Expose an API for token-budget tuning and client-side backpressure hints (they want to call this via SDK config).
- Demo version-pinning + rollout UI in Console; show canary + automatic fallback to smaller model.

Quotes / call snippets:
- CTO: "We need deterministic first-token for tab-complete; end-users abandon suggestions when it lags."
- Lead SWE: "When cache misses happen we see consistent 300-600ms blips — that's the UX killer."
- Product PM: "If you can prove stable TTFT and a good automated token-budget, we'll buy Dedicated."

POC results so far (notes):
- Median TTFT 78ms (good), but p95/p99 tail shows scheduling + cache issues.
- Client saw stuttering when a stream interrupted mid-suggestion -> need streaming resume/backpressure logic.
- Initial Optimize suggestions: smaller batch sizes for low-latency paths, aggressive prefix caching for common imports/snippets, KV prefetch on plugin wake.

Procurement / business notes:
- Interested in 6mo reserved Dedicated pool if we can get p95 < 300ms and SOC2 evidence.
- CFO wants price compare vs self-host (they already evaluated one open-source runtime).

Next steps (short):
- Marco to provision Dedicated microbench config + test script by 2026-03-14.
- Infra to share SOC2 artifact and KMS integration doc by 2026-03-12.
- Priya to coordinate procurement call with CFO week of 2026-03-16.

Blockers: procurement cycle, SOC2 paperwork, VPC egress firewall rules.

Staging notes/obs: keep canary disabled until token-budget tuning implemented.
